_comment: Frozen prompt corpus shared by workloads 1C and 3A. Reproducibility contract: this file is the ONLY source of input text. At runtime each prompt slot i takes base_texts[i % len], tokenizes with the model tokenizer, then tiles (repeats) and truncates the token ids to EXACTLY the target sequence length so input length is fixed and identical every run. The SHA-256 of this file's bytes is recorded in the run metadata JSON. Do not edit between runs that are meant to be comparable.
base_texts: Volta is the GPU microarchitecture NVIDIA introduced in 2017. The V100 accelerator built on it pairs 80 streaming multiprocessors with 32 gigabytes of high bandwidth memory. Each streaming multiprocessor contains independent integer and floating point datapaths and a first generation tensor core capable of a four by four by four mixed precision matrix multiply accumulate per clock. The chip communicates with its peers over six NVLink connections, giving an aggregate bidirectional bandwidth that dwarfs the PCI Express alternative available at the time.

Reproducibility in machine learning benchmarking is less about a single number and more about the conditions under which that number was produced. Fixing the model revision, the tokenizer, the decoding strategy, the batch size, the sequence length, and the library version turns a measurement into something that can be compared across days and across machines. When a comparable measurement drifts, the drift is signal: the only thing that changed was the silicon or its environment.

A key value cache stores the projected keys and values for every token a transformer has already processed so that attention over the growing context does not recompute them. The cache grows linearly with the number of tokens and with the number of layers, and its footprint frequently dominates memory once the prompt is long. Paged attention treats the cache as a set of fixed size blocks managed like virtual memory, which lets a scheduler evict and recompute blocks under pressure rather than failing outright.

Graceful degradation is the property that distinguishes a healthy accelerator from a marginal one when memory is exhausted. A healthy device begins evicting cache blocks, accepts the latency penalty of recomputation, and continues to make forward progress. A marginal device instead exhibits allocation retry storms, pathological latency tails, or a hard out of memory failure. The shape of the response under pressure, not the throughput before it, is the diagnostic.

Greedy decoding selects the highest probability token at every step with no sampling, which removes one large source of run to run variation. It does not by itself guarantee bitwise identical output, because continuous batching can reorder how requests are scheduled and because some reduction kernels are not associative. Disabling cuda graphs, fixing the seed, and constraining concurrency narrows the remaining nondeterminism enough that residual variation can be attributed to the hardware.

Quantization trades numerical precision for memory and sometimes for speed. Eight bit integer weights halve the footprint relative to half precision and, on architectures with the right tensor core support, can also accelerate the matrix multiplies. On older architectures the integer matmul kernels may be absent, in which case the weights are stored compactly but the arithmetic falls back to a wider type, yielding the memory benefit without the compute benefit.

Time to first token measures the latency a user perceives before any output appears. It is dominated by the prefill phase, in which the entire prompt is processed in a single forward pass to populate the key value cache. Longer prompts and larger batches lengthen prefill and therefore lengthen time to first token, which is why the metric is reported alongside the input sequence length that produced it.

Inter token latency measures the cadence of generation after the first token has appeared. It is governed by the decode phase, where one token is produced per step and the cost is dominated by memory bandwidth rather than raw compute. Reporting the median together with the ninety fifth and ninety ninth percentiles exposes the tail behavior that an average alone would conceal, and the tail is where a degrading device reveals itself.

High bandwidth memory stacks dram dies vertically and connects them to the processor through a silicon interposer with a very wide interface. The result is an order of magnitude more bandwidth than a conventional memory subsystem at the cost of fixed capacity that cannot be expanded after manufacture. Because capacity is fixed, a workload sized to the last gigabyte is a deliberate stress test of the memory subsystem and its error correction.

Error correcting codes on a memory subsystem detect and often correct bit flips caused by particle strikes, marginal cells, or aging. A device reporting a slowly rising count of corrected errors is aging gracefully and is still usable. A device reporting uncorrectable errors has crossed a line that no software can paper over, and the health classifier must treat the two cases as categorically different.

Tensor parallelism splits the weight matrices of a single model across several devices so that one forward pass is a coordinated effort with collective communication at every layer. It increases the model size that fits but couples the devices, so a fault on one is felt by all. Replicating an independent copy of the model on every device instead keeps the devices isolated, which is the right choice when the goal is to grade each device on its own.

A thermal ramp is the transient period at the start of a sustained workload during which the silicon and its cooling solution have not yet reached equilibrium. Throughput measured during the ramp is contaminated by clocks that are still boosting and temperatures that are still climbing. Discarding the first minute and scoring only the steady state isolates the property of interest, which is sustained behavior rather than peak behavior.

The streaming multiprocessor clock is the frequency at which the compute datapaths advance. Under a sustained load a healthy device settles at a stable boost clock dictated by its power and thermal limits. A clock that sags over time, or that oscillates, points to a power delivery or cooling problem that will surface as throughput variance long before it becomes an outright failure.

Continuous batching is the scheduling discipline that lets new requests join an in flight batch as soon as earlier requests finish, rather than waiting for an entire batch to complete. It keeps the device saturated and improves aggregate throughput, but it makes the per request timeline depend on the company a request keeps. Honest latency reporting therefore attributes timestamps per request rather than per batch.

A power virus is a synthetic workload constructed to maximize the switching activity of the silicon and therefore its power draw, well beyond what a realistic application would sustain. It is useful for characterizing the worst case thermal and electrical behavior of a device, but it is not representative of inference, and conflating the two leads to capacity planning that is either wasteful or unsafe.

The point of an integrated baseline is to exercise compute, memory bandwidth, the full attention mechanism, the cache allocator, and the scheduler at the same time, because faults often live in the interaction between subsystems rather than in any one of them. Isolated microbenchmarks find a weak datapath, but only the integrated workload reveals a weak interaction, and interactions are where aging silicon tends to break first.
